questions.stem: India's first solar observatory mission is:
questions.explanation: Aditya-L1 (launched 2 Sept 2023, reached L1 on 6 Jan 2024) is India's first dedicated solar-observation mission.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The G20 Summit in 2023 was held in:
questions.explanation: The 2023 G20 Summit was held in New Delhi (Sept 9-10, 2023) during India's G20 presidency. The Leaders' Declaration was a notable diplomatic outcome. 2024 summit was in Brazil; 2025 in South Africa.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Consider the following about India's 2024 Lok Sabha composition. 1. The total elected strength is 543 members. 2. 84 seats are reserved for Scheduled Castes. 3. 47 seats are reserved for Scheduled Tribes. 4. Anglo-Indian nominated members are still part of the House. Which are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement 4 is WRONG — the Anglo-Indian nomination provision was DISCONTINUED by the 104th Amendment (2019), effective 25 Jan 2020. The present Lok Sabha has NO nominated Anglo-Indians. Statements 1-3 are correct: 543 elected, 84 SC, 47 ST.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: India achieved its 'Tiger Reserve' status for Kaziranga in:
questions.explanation: Kaziranga declared a Tiger Reserve in 2006. It was established as a National Park in 1974, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1985, and a Tiger Reserve in 2006 under Project Tiger.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Consider the following statements about India's NATIONAL EMBLEM (the Ashokan lion capital of Sarnath). 1. It was adopted as the State Emblem of India on 26 January 1950. 2. It contains four Asiatic lions seated back-to-back on a circular abacus. 3. The abacus has four smaller animals: horse, bull, elephant, lion, separated by intervening wheels (Dharma Chakras). 4. Below the abacus, the national motto 'Satyameva Jayate' is inscribed in Devanagari. Which are correct?
questions.explanation: All four correct. The original capital (currently at Sarnath Museum) is from c. 250 BCE. The State Emblem adopted on R-Day 1950 shows only three lions visible (the 4th is hidden behind), but there are four lions in total. 'Satyameva Jayate' is from the Mundaka Upanishad (III.1.6).

questions.stem: Which of the following pairs of INDIAN NATIONAL SYMBOLS is INCORRECTLY matched?

options.option_text: National Aquatic Animal — River Dolphin (Ganges dolphin)

questions.explanation: National flower of India is the LOTUS (Nelumbo nucifera), not mango blossom. Mango blossoms are associated with Bengali New Year etc. The other pairings are correct. (National Animal — Bengal Tiger; National Bird — Peacock; National Fruit — Mango; National River — Ganga; National Aquatic Animal — Gangetic Dolphin, declared in 2009; National Heritage Animal — Indian Elephant, declared 2010.)
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Match the international organisation with its HEADQUARTERS. A. IMF. B. World Bank. C. WHO. D. WTO. List-II: 1. Washington D.C. 2. Washington D.C. 3. Geneva. 4. Geneva.
questions.explanation: IMF and World Bank are both headquartered in Washington DC (Bretton Woods institutions). WHO is in Geneva (1948). WTO also Geneva (1995). Though matching 1 and 2 to two different places is visually confusing, the correctness is: all four pair up as shown in option A.
